**B01AF01** is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for rivaroxaban, a direct oral anticoagulant ([[doac|DOAC]]) [^src1]. In the Danish healthcare system, this drug code is centrally tracked to monitor the quality of care for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1]. Specifically, B01AF01 is encompassed by national clinical quality indicators that measure both the initiation of [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]] and the necessary monitoring of renal function in these patients [^src1].

The code is part of a broader standardized coding framework used by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to evaluate cardiovascular care [^src3]. Within the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK) reports, B01AF01 is consistently grouped with other oral anticoagulants. These include vitamin K antagonists ([[b01aa|B01AA]]), dabigatran ([[b01ae07|B01AE07]]), apixaban ([[b01af02|B01AF02]]), and edoxaban ([[b01af03|B01AF03]]) [^src4]. The tracking of these specific ATC codes allows health authorities to calculate precise metrics, such as the waiting time for anticoagulation therapy and the rates of complications like ischemic stroke or severe bleeding [^src5]. 

Documentation of B01AF01 appears across multiple annual AFDK reports from 2023 through 2025, reflecting its ongoing role as a technical reference for clinical quality measurement and registry analysis in Denmark [^src2].
